ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 as amended (Panama AML/CFT framework); Decree 363 of 2015 and related implementing regulations of the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities (today within the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities, formerly UAF); Law 52 of 2016 regarding bearer shares; Executive Decree 951 of 2017 establishing beneficial ownership information to be maintained by legal entities; Resolution SBP-OSS 005-2018 of the Superintendency of Banks; and Consolidated Text of the Public Registry regulations on foundations (Ley 25 de 2018 and reforms under Law 190 of 2021, concerning UBO registers administered by the Registro Público de Panamá). The private interest foundation statute is Law 25 of 12 June 1995, as amended by Law 12 of 2019 and Law 69 of 2021.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the founder, members of the foundation council, beneficiaries, and any protector against: (1) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and country-specific sanctions programs; (2) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (3) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) the Public Registry of Panama's in-house money laundering and terrorism financing risk indicators; (5) the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities risk classification matrices for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates; and (6) domestic Panamanian AML/CFT list for high-risk jurisdictions, all under Law 23 of 2015 Articles 36-44 and the Financial Action Task Force Recommendations 12 and 22 implementation standards. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds documentation and senior management approval, is required where the UBO is a PEP, where sanctions-list hits are detected, or where the contribution involves high-risk jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sistema de Reserva de Nombre y Constitución de Fundaciones (online platform via registropublico.gob.pa and the 'Sistema de Fundaciones de Interés Privado' module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name may be in Spanish or any foreign language, but under Public Registry practice all names must be transliterated into Latin script for registry indexing; any name using non-Latin characters must be accompanied by an official transliteration; the name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered Panamanian entity, trademark, or foundation; a Spanish-language version may be required for administrative clarity where the primary name is in a non-Spanish language; prohibited abbreviations of corporate types and terms referring to banking, insurance, securities, or public enterprises require prior authorization.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Prohibited terms implying public utility, monetary authority, central bank, or state-owned enterprises; terms requiring prior ministerial or regulatory approval under Law 25 of 1995, the Banking Law, the Insurance Code, and the Securities Law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or its resident agent may file a written administrative reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Directora General del Registro Público within five business days of notification; the petition must specify the legal basis and include a revised proposed name if the objection is based on similarity; if the objection is founded on a prohibited token, the applicant may alternatively submit a prior ministerial or regulatory authorization accompanied by evidence of approval from the relevant authority (e.g., Superintendency of Banks or Superintendency of Securities); if the reconsideration is denied, an appeal may be filed before the Tribunal Administrativo Tributario o jurisdictional administrative courts, or in the alternative a fresh name reservation may be submitted with a modified admissible name, subject to payment of a new reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Panama is mandatory for the foundation, and must be a physical address, typically provided by a licensed resident agent; virtual office services are accepted strictly for administrative correspondence but do not replace the statutory resident agent's physical office; for ISIC 5229 heavy haul and project cargo logistics with no statutory license requirement, the Public Registry and AML/CFT supervisors accept a resident agent's physical office as the registered office; however, banking relationship managers and the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities generally require a substantive operational address where management records, contracts, and UBO documentation are physically accessible; purely virtual or co-working addresses without a designated local service relationship are assessed as insufficient for the foundation's register of documents and for demonstrating economic substance under territorial tax rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% to 40% quantifiable risk for newly incorporated private interest foundations in the project cargo logistics industry where the resident agent serves as a single-service provider without demonstrating local operational substance; physical inspection probability increases to approximately 60% where foreign management, high transaction values, or jurisdictions on high-risk lists are present; foundations with fully outsourced local administration and no physical local director office face elevated unannounced inspection risk; the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities and the Public Registry conduct periodic targeted inspections and may require the production of UBO registers, foundation agreements, and accounting support within five to ten business days.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Act), as amended by Ley No. 13 de 2017; arts. 1-25 on constitution, endowment, registration; arts. 26-35 on foundation council, protector, and supervening events
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General de Registro Público, Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta de Constitución / Escritura de Fundación de Interés Privado) filed for annotation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of US$10,000 or equivalent assets, evidenced by a bank certificate or sworn asset declaration and placed under control of the foundation council before registry annotation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED unanimously: (1) The foundation is constituted under Ley 25 de 1995, as amended, and accepts the initial endowment of US$10,000 contributed by the Founder. (2) The registered office at [Panama City address] is adopted as the foundation’s legal domicile. (3) The provisional Foundation Council is approved and the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer. (4) The Council is authorised to open bank accounts, sign banking instructions, and engage licensed professional agent services. (5) All filings before the Public Registry are ratified and confirmed. (6) This resolution takes effect immediately and shall be entered into the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Registered Agent and Drafting of Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panama registered agent and Panamanian notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the registered agent to prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish reflecting founder, endowment, council, beneficiaries, and registered office. Notarize the charter before a Panamanian notary and obtain the registered agent acceptance form.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder’s passport or corporate ID
Certified good-standing certificate for corporate founder, if applicable
Bank balance letter or asset statement proving US$10,000 endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects due to name conflict, reserve a new name with the Public Registry and re-execute the charter at no substantive defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Foundation Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter through the Public Registry’s physical or online window for annotation, pay the registration fee, and present the name reservation certificate together with the charter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice, correct the indicated item within 10 business days by filing an amendment note or supplementary evidence and restart review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Tax Identification Number and Municipal Operating Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipio de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the registry annotation certificate to apply for RUC (tax identification number). After RUC issuance, apply for the municipal commercial operating notice at the municipality corresponding to the registered office and pay the modest municipal tax.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries economic activity classification, file an activity explanation referencing ISIC 5229 and re-submit; obtain amended municipal license following corrected classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Corporate Bank Account and Endowment Endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama-licensed commercial bank supervised by Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the registry certificate, RUC, foundation charter, council resolution, and beneficial ownership declaration to the bank’s corporate desk. Complete customer due diligence, deposit or evidence the minimum endowment, and secure the bank certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced due diligence, provide sworn source-of-funds evidence and personal tax returns of officers; escalate to the bank’s compliance committee for final approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and Gaceta Oficial / Official Gazette if publication required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm completion of any required registry publication, pay publication fees, obtain the final certificate of registration and certified copy of the annotated charter, and maintain all corporate records at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance of the standing certificate is delayed, request an urgent certified copy and written status letter; rely on provisional annotation for third-party dealings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies; optional logistics activity registration may be made at Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias for heavy cargo support services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial Operating Notice (Aviso de Operación) issued by Municipio de Panamá

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — corporate project-cargo logistics brokerage with no physical manufacturing, construction, or terminal operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at pure brokerage stage; any future warehouse or terminal handling facility must comply with MiAMBIENTE Resolution No. 061-2018 category II thresholds and Executive Decree No. 379 de 2006 on wastewater discharges and waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No structural or fire-safety certification is required for pure project-cargo logistics coordination; if an office or temporary staging yard is occupied, obtain a fire inspection certificate from Dirección General de Bomberos and ordinary workplace safety clearance under Panama’s occupational health rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; primary digital portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa with institutional site https://www.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or domestic vehicle (including a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995) must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) before conducting taxable activities. Procedure: (1) pre-registration appointment at the DGI Sede Electrónica; (2) submission of foundation charter, public deed, authentic certificate of existence issued by the Registro Público de Panamá, identity documents of the Consejo de Fundación and the appointed agente residente; (3) evidence of registered legal address in Panama; (4) RUC application and simultaneous ITBMS registration; (5) issuance of RUC certificate together with tax ID credential and digital certificate enabling e-filing and electronic invoicing. A PIF may obtain a RUC as a non-commercial holding vehicle; however, if the PIF itself carries out Panamanian-source commercial activities, full income tax and ITBMS registration obligations apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no US-style check-the-box election and no OECD hybrid mismatch election. The PIF is a separate legal person taxed only on Panamanian-source income under territorial rules; foreign-source income and capital gains are outside the Panamanian tax net absent remittance of funds to Panamanian territory in a taxable manner. Available statutory elections include: (i) entry into the Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes for gross annual income not exceeding USD/PAB 150,000, which permits simplified ITBMS and income tax compliance; (ii) registration under the Panama-Pacifico Special Economic Area or a free-zone regime for logistics operators to obtain customs and tax privileges; (iii) maintenance of separately identified Panamanian-source and foreign-source revenue accounts in statutory records to substantiate territorial exemption; (iv) no entity-level election converts a PIF into a full taxable corporation unless the foundation's charter is amended to perform systematic commercial activities in Panama, in which case the foundation becomes a normal taxpayer under the Código Fiscal.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a las Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) - Panama's VAT/GST equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general statutory monetary threshold for ITBMS registration; any person transferring movable goods or providing services in Panamanian territory is subject to ITBMS and must register with the DGI. A special small-taxpayer regime (Régimen Especial de Pequeños Contribuyentes) applies where gross annual income does not exceed PAB/USD 150,000, allowing simplified quarterly payment instead of full monthly ITBMS filing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) through DGI-authorized software platforms integrated with the Sede Electrónica. Taxpayers transmit invoices in near-real time using XML with a fiscally certified digital certificate; the DGI assigns a sequential authorization code to each issued invoice, serving as digital clearance. There is no physical fiscal printer stamping. The e-invoicing mandate was rolled out progressively by taxpayer category from 2021 through 2025; logistics and project-cargo operators with active ITBMS registration must issue electronic invoices to Panamanian clients and may receive e-invoices from local suppliers to substantiate input credits. Non-resident service providers without a local establishment must appoint a local fiscal representative or use an approved e-invoicing operator to comply when invoicing Panamanian counterparties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS applies at 0% to exports of goods and qualifying offshore services. Eligibility requirements: (1) tangible goods, including out-of-gauge heavy-lift project cargo, depart Panama under a customs export declaration evidencing physical exit; (2) services are rendered to non-resident customers for consumption or use outside Panama, such as international freight forwarding, heavy-lift logistics, and project cargo management performed predominantly abroad; (3) the transaction is documented with contracts, commercial invoices and shipping instruments demonstrating the cross-border nature; (4) the seller retains export documentation and foreign-currency remittance evidence. Input ITBMS incurred in respect of exempt or zero-rated export operations is creditable, and any residual monthly credit balance (saldo a favor) may be carried forward or claimed as a refund from the DGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanera - DUA)
Bill of Lading (ocean or through bill covering OOG heavy-lift carriage)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank certificate evidencing receipt of foreign funds)
Commercial Invoice and signed project cargo / freight services contract
Packing list, OOG surveyor or weight certificate, and dangerous goods declaration where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may scrutinize export zero-rating and refund claims within the statute of limitations of up to five years, extended for fraud cases. Where zero-rating is disallowed, the DGI will claw back the credited input ITBMS and issue unsettled assessments, plus a 10% monthly surcharge (recargo) capped by law, statutory interest of 1% per month on the unpaid balance, and / or fines of up to 100% of the omitted tax. Fraudulent export claims involving falsified invoices, false export declarations or simulated foreign counterparts give rise to criminal sanctions under both the Código Fiscal and Código Penal, including customs fraud and aggravated tax evasion penalties. Liability may extend jointly and severally to the foundation council and the resident agent if they knowingly participated in the use of false export documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, SBP) exercises statutory banking supervision, prudential oversight, and AML/CFT enforcement under Cabinet Decree 238 of 1970, Legislative Decree 2 of 2008, and Decree 168 of 2013 (as amended). The Banco Nacional de Panama operates as fiscal agent of the State and local clearing agent; monetary policy is effectively that of the U.S. Federal Reserve because the U.S. Dollar is the only circulating legal tender. The Panamanian Balboa exists solely as a nominal unit for fractional coins at fixed 1:1 parity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both capital and current account; the economy is completely dollarized, so no central exchange-control authority or reference-rate apparatus exists. There are no statutory restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, capital repatriation, or liquidation proceeds for a Private Interest Foundation or corporate treasury holding USD accounts. Payouts are subject solely to general AML reporting thresholds (UAF/Official Financial Analysis Unit) and, where applicable, territorial taxation rules; foreign-source logistics income (heavy-haul freight, charter, demurrage) is freely remittable without source tax or prior approval. Non-USD exposures (EUR, CNY, GBP, COP) clear freely through commercial banks at market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no mandatory surrender regime, no statutory timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds or service receipts (ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510 project cargo logistics). Freight, charter hire, BAF, port handling, and OOG survey revenues may be retained in USD in any licensed Panama bank, applied to working capital, or routed offshore without central-bank authorization. Prudent practice under Decree 168 of 2013 is to retain underlying invoices and bank statements for at least five years to support transaction justification before the UAF if requested.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.regulatory_observation_notice: Panama was removed from the FATF grey list in October 2023; nevertheless, SBP continues enhanced due diligence enforcement on non-resident investment vehicles. The PIF must maintain its registered agent, resident legal counsel, and updated foundation books to avoid de-risking by Tier-1 banks.

Operational USD current account; trade finance desk for LC confirmations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM for treasury-grade clearing, MEDIUM as supplementary collection channel. SBP Agreement No. 008-2021 created a permissive Electronic Money Entity (Empresas de Dinero Electronico) licensing regime and the SBP Fintech Innovation Hub offers a sandbox, but these licensed EMIs do not yet operate as primary correspondent clearing nodes for project cargo logistics. Offshore digital EMIs (UK/EU electronic-money institutions such as Wise, Currencycloud, or Airwallex) can legally collect and disburse funds in Panama only through their own correspondent relationships; they cannot hold a Panama nostro or clearing membership, and their use tends to lengthen KYC review at Tier-1 banks because of the layered payment chain. Recommended posture: use EMIs only for low-value disbursements to sub-contractors or surveyors with a clear invoice trail; retain SWIFT MT103 direct rails for all high-value milestone and LC-backed transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of at least one foundation council member or an authorized signatory is the baseline rule at most Tier-1 banks (Banco General, Banistmo, Multibank, Credicorp). Towerbank and select private-bank desks permit a 'remote-in-person' protocol: digital submission of apostilled foundation deed (pacto fundacional), notarized consular certified passports, a sworn source-of-funds declaration, two professional reference letters, and a live video interview before compliance; final signature legalization must still be executed before a Panamanian notary or through the PIF's resident registered agent in Panama City. Full remote opening for a foundation without an in-country counsel or registered agent is effectively unavailable. Budget 10-20 business days for onboarding regardless of the chosen route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation beneficial-ownership opacity; foundation charter does not publicly disclose beneficiaries or protectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unredacted foundation deed with notarial cachet; Panamanian registered-agent legal opinion citing Law 25 of 1995 and Decree 168 of 2013; complete chain of foundation council members, protector, and named beneficiary; sworn statement of source of assets and funds; certified copy of foundation registry inscription (Registro Publico).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of economic substance in Panama (CRS/FATCA mismatch, tax-haven label).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of office lease for registered address; retained legal counsel agreement; board or council minutes for the foundation; local administrator or registered-agent confirmation; Panama ITBMS (VAT-equivalent) filing receipts; evidence of actual contract negotiation or logistics management performed in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex cross-border treasury flows typical of OOG heavy-haul: interconnected payments across project sites, foreign charterers, and heavy-equipment suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Project contracts with milestone schedules; purchase orders for heavy-lift trailers or special equipment; commercial invoices; AIB/CWB (airway or bill of lading) or port terminal receipts; OOG surveyor reports; mapping of each wire to specific deliverable; signed contractual flow chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment instruction (client or charterer directs PIF to pay a supplier not party to the original contract).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed indemnity and authorization letter; supplier invoice; underlying contract clause permitting substitution; non-recourse acknowledgment from the third party; corporate-to-corporate payment only (no personal accounts); full beneficial chain of the third-party supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-wide AML concern in shipping/logistics: risk of sanctions evasion, dual-use cargo, or misleading beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFSI/OFAC/UN sanctions screening results for all counterparties; P&I Club insurance certificate; CTPAT or equivalent security certificate; two trade reference letters from established logistics counterparties; customs broker declarations for each high-risk cargo class; compliance manual adopted by the foundation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Approved protocol: (1) Sponsor or beneficial owner initiates SWIFT MT103 from an account held in their own name to the PIF's USD operating account at the chosen Panama Tier-1 bank; (2) Field 70 of the MT103 must state expressly 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION' plus reference to the specific foundation deed article authorizing the initial patrimony or subsequent capital increase; (3) for items above USD 50,000, the bank applies enhanced sanctions/wire screening, and the PIF must pre-supply a capital contribution certificate signed by the council and verified by legal counsel; (4) local Panama-to-Panama transfers may be routed through the SIP (Sistema de Pagos Interbancarios) RTGS operated by SBP clearing stations to reduce correspondent fees; (5) all injections are journaled to the foundation's internal equity/capital sub-account and applied only to project working capital, never commingled with personal receipts. Use of a documented internal capital ledger is essential for later distributable earnings calculations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rail suite: (A) SWIFT MT103 for freight payments, port handling, BAF, surveyor fees, and independent subcontractor settlement, citing purpose narrative 'Trade settlement for heavy-haul project cargo logistics services'; (B) MT202 COVER for correspondent funding in back-to-back documentary credit arrangements; (C) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) issued by the client's or charterer's bank and confirmed by the Panama Tier-1 bank for large heavy-lift vessel charters or specialised equipment purchases; (D) Documentary collections (DP/DA) with drafts for contractual milestone amounts where LC terms are unavailable; (E) ISO 20022 structured payment details for subcontractor sweeps above USD 250,000, accompanied by a signed statement of trade value and, when requested, HS classification aligned with ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510. All outbound flows must map to an underlying project master file of invoices and contractual clauses to satisfy UAF and internal audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contract (vanilla, physical delivery): 1-week to 12-month tenors on USD/CNY, USD/EUR, USD/GBP via Tier-1 treasury desks to hedge heavy equipment purchases and charter payments.
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS): 6-24 month USD/CNY or USD/EUR swaps matching milestone receipts and contractor disbursement schedules.
FX Option (OTC Puts/Calls): zero-premium collars and risk reversals to cap adverse Euro or Renminbi movement on budgeted project revenues.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF): available indirectly through global correspondents for hedges against Colombian Peso, Mexican Peso, or other non-fully convertible Latin American currencies arising from regional heavy-haul expansion.

USD-Liquidity Sweep and Reverse Repurchase on US Treasury securities: not a classic FX hedge but permissible treasury instrument to smooth daily clearing balances at the Panama clearing bank and manage funding of MT103 disbursement spikes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_clearing_notes: Deployment order for operational liquidity: (1) USD balances held at Tier-1 Panama bank, up to federal deposit protection via FDLI or Swiss-style private placement (Panama has no equivalent deposit insurance; use diversification across two Tier-1 banks); (2) same-day USD clearing via SIP and ACH Panama, operated under SBP and the Asociacion Bancaria de Panama; (3) highest-value cross-border payments via correspondent banks (BONY, JP Morgan, Citi, HSBC) with pre-advice to the compliance officer 48 hours before settlement; (4) restriction that no cryptocurrency or digital-asset clearing rail is permitted for project cargo trade settlements under this treasury mandate unless expressly authorized under SBP sandbox protocol.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Annual Treasury Fee / Aviso Anual de Operación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá through the Registered Agent; tax component administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year; payments made after the deadline are subject to surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% surcharge plus delay penalties; failure to pay for three consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off / cancellation of the Foundation certificate by the Public Registry, subject to reinstatement procedures and additional fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent designated for the Foundation; updated registration in the Beneficial Ownership Registry maintained by the Registro Público de Panamá (not a public filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at the Foundation's registration anniversary or as requested by the Registered Agent; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain accurate and current UBO records may subject the Foundation and the Registered Agent to fines up to USD 20,000 under Law 129 of 2020; persistent non-compliance may result in administrative cancellation of the Foundation's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (only if the Foundation generates Panamanian-source commercial income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the chosen fiscal year; no filing obligation for a dormant foundation or a foundation with only foreign-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For active Panamanian-source operations, late or non-filing triggers fines under the Fiscal Code, denial of deductions, and potential tax reassessments; administrative penalties increase progressively for extended non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. However, if the Foundation undertakes regulated activities, conducts commercial operations within Panama that exceed the thresholds established by the DGI, or is specifically designated by a Panama court or the Tax Authority, audited financial statements may be required; otherwise unaudited internal accounts are sufficient.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (full IFRS) for entities required to present financial statements; foundations without filing obligations may maintain records under IFRS or simplified local GAAP, provided the books accurately reflect assets, liabilities, income, and expenditures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Registered Agent must verify and confirm the Foundation's beneficial ownership information at least once a year, obtaining a signed affirmation from the Foundation Council. Any transfer of beneficial interests, amendment to foundation charter, or change of beneficiaries must be reported to the Registered Agent within 30 days. No annual government return is required for unchanged PIFs, but the internal UBO register must remain current and be available for inspection by Panamanian authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Final Beneficiaries (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions
Register of Endowed Assets and Liabilities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 450 per annum depending on service provider and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - USD 2,500; not a statutory requirement for a standard PIF, only incurred when a client-directed certification is needed or Panamanian-source activities require audited statements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Private Interest Foundations (Law 25 of 1995, Arts. 42-46) benefit from a territorial tax exclusion: income derived from assets or rights situated outside Panama and distributions to beneficiaries are entirely exempt from Panamanian income, inheritance, and gift tax. Panama-source active logistics revenue attracts the standard 25% head-rate. No general statutory tax holiday applies; incentives are limited to regime-specific exemptions such as the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) program.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 820 (Declaracion Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) for juridical persons, filed electronically through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 portal (Oficina Virtual de la DGI, Direccion General de Ingresos).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is March 31. No general statutory extension is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) identifier of the Private Interest Foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the foundation RUC; a Panamanian registered agent and fiscal representation are mandatory for non-resident settlors.
Calendar year for standard PIFs unless a different fiscal year was authorized by the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue accrued or received in the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all global logistics billing; foreign-source project-cargo revenue is segregated as exempt in the following line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt and foreign-source income (rentas exentas y de fuente extranjera).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare revenue from haulage and logistics services physically performed outside Panama, supported by bills of lading, polizas, and milestone certificates, to evidence territorial exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source taxable revenue (renta de fuente panamena).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only services performed, loading/unloading, warehousing, or inland carriage that occurs inside Panama; zero if operations are wholly extraterritorial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after cost of sales and deductible operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs may deduct only expenses directly connected with Panama-source income; foreign costs are non-allocable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss carryforward (Loss carryforward: maximum 5 years, no carryback).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only against Panama-source income; losses from foreign operations are disregarded.
Zero when the PIF realizes only foreign-source income; the territorial doctrine is self-executing but must be evidenced on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits and quarterly advance payments (anticipos).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits apply only to Panama-source invoices; foreign-client LCs are outside the Panamanian withholding net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle by wire in USD via the DGI collection network; overpayments may be carried forward or refunded on application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: fine of USD 50.00 to USD 500.00 (Fiscal Code Art. 711). Late payment: surcharge of 10% on the unpaid tax for the first month plus 1.5% per additional month or fraction, capped at 30%, with moratory interest of 1% per month. False or understated returns: penalty of 25% of the underdeclared tax; fraudulent returns attract penalties of 100% to 300% of the omitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Panama general corporate dividend withholding: 5% on dividends paid from Panama-source taxable income; 10% on distributions from non-taxable or exempt income to recipients resident abroad (Fiscal Code Arts. 302, 302-A). PIF special rule: beneficiary distributions from foreign-source endowment are exempt from all Panamanian tax, inheritance tax, and gift tax, resulting in an effective 0% Panamanian WHT where the underlying assets are outside Panama.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief under Panama's tax treaties (in force with Mexico, Luxembourg, Singapore, Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, France, UK, UAE, South Korea, Czech Republic, Ireland, Italy, Barbados, Qatar, Vietnam, among others) requires: (i) obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the counterparty tax authority; (ii) filing the DGI international request form with a certified Spanish or English translation, audited proof of beneficial ownership, and a copy of the underlying contractual flow; (iii) an administrative resolution from the DGI International Tax Directorate authorizing the reduced rate or refund; and (iv) annual recertification. No unilateral domestic relief exists for treaty-shopping structures lacking economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties, trademarks, patents, and technical assistance paid to non-residents: 12.5% (Fiscal Code Art. 300). Interest remitted abroad: 5% when the creditor is a foreign banking institution; 12.5% for unrelated non-resident lenders. Treaty-reduced rates commonly set royalties at 10% and interest at 5% to 10% (e.g., Mexico, Luxembourg, Singapore, South Korea), subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership verification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 12,000,000 (Panama's official currency is the Balboa at 1:1 parity with the U.S. dollar) in annual gross revenue, or related-party transactions exceeding USD 3,000,000 in a fiscal year, triggers mandatory Master File and Local File documentation under Law 58 of 2017, Executive Decree 24 of 2018, and DGI Resolution 201-2974.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 254 of 2021 (Regulated by Decree 163 of 2022) applies the OECD economic substance standard to all Panamanian legal vehicles, including PIFs. The project-cargo heavy-haul logistics scope (ISIC 5229 / distribution and logistics services) is a 'relevant activity' requiring: local management and board meetings in Panama, a physical office, adequate qualified staff, and core income-generating activity in Panama. A PIF that is tax-resident and compliant in a foreign jurisdiction may satisfy the doctrine through verified foreign tax residence; otherwise, the PIF must annually file substance information and pay a substance fee. Failure renders the vehicle liable to recharacterization, information exchange, and fines up to USD 1,000,000 for serious infringements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panama-source project-cargo revenue, use of double invoicing, false deductions, or concealment of payments settled by letter of credit in order to reduce the taxable base to zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 70 of 2019 criminalizes tax evasion with imprisonment of three (3) to five (5) years for simple evasion and five (5) to seven (7) years for aggravated evasion, plus fines of five (5) to ten (10) times the evaded tax, closure of the establishment, and forfeiture of instrumentalities. Fiscal Code Arts. 705-707 additionally impose civil penalties of 100% to 300% of the omitted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the foundation's registered agents are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded taxes, may be barred from holding corporate office for up to 10 years, and face personal imprisonment under Law 70 of 2019; preventative travel bans (inhibicion de salida) and asset freezes are routinely ordered during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Panama PIF with no physical office, no local employees, no board meetings in Panama, and no foreign tax residence, while executing heavy-haul logistics contracts through nominee service providers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 254 of 2021 and Decree 163 of 2022 impose graduated administrative fines from USD 10,000 up to USD 1,000,000 for failure to prove economic substance, fraudulent substance declarations, or incomplete annual substance filings; the DGI may also strike the foundation from the register and automatically exchange its information with foreign tax authorities under the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the foundation council are personally liable for the substance filing obligations; knowing participation in a sham vehicle triggers civil liability for all unpaid taxes and penalties, suspension from acting as director in Panama, and criminal exposure for false declarations before the DGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash, bearer instruments, or funds routed through unvetted third parties for project-cargo freight, knowingly invoicing to shell clients designated on sanctions lists, or using the PIF to obscure beneficial ownership of cargo payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 (AML), Criminal Code Art. 254: money laundering carries imprisonment of five (5) to ten (10) years, increased to ten (10) to fifteen (15) years in aggravated circumstances, fines of up to USD 10,000,000, asset forfeiture, and administrative sanctions by the Intendencia de Supervision y Fiscalizacion; the freight logistics sector is an obliged non-financial entity required to maintain customer due diligence and suspicious-transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are directly indictable as co-authors for laundering through the PIF; personal asset freezes, five-year travel bans, extradition exposure, and civil restitution orders apply; the corporate veil is pierced as a matter of course where the foundation is found to be a conduit for illicit cargo payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border payments between the Panamanian PIF and related logistics affiliates (intercompany haulage commissions, equipment leases, service fees) exceeding the USD 12,000,000 revenue threshold without preparing Master File, Local File, or benchmarking analysis, or refusing DGI access to related-party records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal Code Art. 762-K: fines of USD 10,000 to USD 30,000 for non-submission of transfer-pricing documentation, plus adjusted assessments and interest; the DGI may disregard the transaction and re-characterize the PIF's profit at the 25% head-rate with a 10% to 30% accuracy surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve related-party contracts knowing they depart from arm's length are jointly liable for the resulting tax adjustment and fines; repeated non-cooperation constitutes tax fraud under Law 70 of 2019 with personal custodial exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Formulario 820, non-payment of quarterly advance payments, or failure to withhold the 12.5% WHT on royalties and the 5%/10% dividend WHT when distributing Panama-source profits to non-resident beneficiaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing fine of USD 50 to USD 500; late-payment surcharge of 10% for the first month plus 1.5% per month (capped at 30%); moratory interest of 1% per month; withholding agents that fail to remit WHT are liable for 100% of the unwithheld amount plus penalties of 25% to 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Fiscal Code Art. 124, directors and officers are personally and severally liable for unremitted withholdings, regardless of the foundation's insolvency; DGI enforcement includes personal asset attachment, travel restrictions, and disqualification from managing Panamanian entities; criminal liability arises where the default is fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing Formulario 820 with inflated foreign-source exemption, fabricated freight invoices, fake cost deductions, or misrepresenting the PIF's foreign tax residence to the DGI and counterparty treaty authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal Code Art. 713 and Law 70 of 2019: fines of 100% to 300% of the omitted tax; aggravated tax evasion imprisonment of five (5) to seven (7) years; confiscation of assets derived from the fraud; and automatic publication of the sanction in the Official Gazette.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers and the registered agent face personal criminal prosecution, subsidiary liability for all fiscal debts, debarment from practicing as agent in Panama, and, for forged foreign TRCs, international mutual legal assistance requests resulting in extradition.
